paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jehoram walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and the house of Ahab, because he married Ahab's daughter (2 Chronicles 21:6). The text puts those two things side by side. Who we walk beside, and whose ways we copy, shapes where our feet end up.

Now look at what Elijah's letter says. The LORD names what Jehoram did, and He names what's coming (2 Chronicles 21:12-15). Jehoram forsook the LORD, and the rebellions, the invasion and the sickness all followed (2 Chronicles 21:10, 16-19). God takes sin seriously, even when the sinner is wearing a crown. And in the end Jehoram died "to no one's regret," which is a heavy way to be remembered (2 Chronicles 21:20).

But don't miss the lamp, friend. Jehoram was doing evil, and still the LORD was unwilling to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant He had made with David (2 Chronicles 21:7). God keeps His promises even when the people He promised to are a mess. So the question for you today is this: whose ways are you walking in, and are you leaning on a God who keeps His word? I'd pick Him every time, and my oven timer agrees.
